reasons: The change delivers the intent and all nine clauses, with no non-goal crossed: no client-side script, no settings-file read, no search. The lane ledger shows no lanes ran, but the executable checks report no witness missing or failing and every target witness killed under mutation. I also ran the full suite locally at this head: 68 pass, 0 fail.
A1 met: free books get a link with a visually hidden title, and held books get none. T-4 passes and the shelf capture at 360px looks right.
A2 met: the confirmation words the end from the stored reservedUntil and shows the book and address but no name. T-20 and the settings test cover it.
A3 met: one visible field and a hidden token; the confirmation has no form and one link. T-28 covers it.
A4 met: 409 with M3 and a link to /. Bytes, inode and mtime are unchanged and no stray files remain. T-6 covers it.
A5 met: blank, whitespace and zero-width names get a 400 with the same book's form and no write. T-7 covers it.
A6 met: the check and write sit together inside updateShelf. T-32 sees one 303 and nineteen 409s, and the file holds the winner's name.
A7 met: `now` is read per request and defaults to the system clock. The exact end still holds, one millisecond later the book is free and can be reserved again, and T-18 and T-2 hold.

A8 met: 404 M2, 503 M6 with Retry-After, the 60 code-point limit and control-character refusals, esc on every new page, and a 413 without reading the whole body. My experiment with a real client sending a 5MB body got the 413 page. An aborted upload logs only 'aborted', with no name.
A9 met: the POST answers 303, a same-token repeat redirects with no write (inode checked), a different token gets 409, and concurrent same-token POSTs all get 303.

Persistence and redaction reviewed: refusals throw so nothing is saved, the hold end comes from the moment of the write under the lock, and claims survive in the file across restarts. No name appears in a Location header, a log or any GET page; only the neighbour's own typed value returns on their own refused form.

UI reviewed from the builder's 360px captures of the shelf, M4 and the confirmation: no sideways scroll on b1's long URL, a dashed refusal and a solid confirmation, the paper, ink and rust palette, and the refusal first in main. The M3 capture exists but I did not open it. Lettered fonts fall back in the capture environment; the CSS stack is unchanged.
